nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Among this is His words, Majestic and Mighty, (بَراءَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ).
It is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (إِلَى الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ). Beginning with an indefinite noun is acceptable because it has been qualified [by what follows it]. It is also permissible for «براءة» to be nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. One says: bariʾtu from the covenant, from the religion and from the man, barāʾa (disavowal); and baraʾtu from illness, abraʾu — and no faʿaltu/afʿalu pattern is known among verbs whose third radical is hamza except this one; and one also says: bariʾtu from illness, abraʾu, burʾan and buruʾan. And baraytu the pen (I sharpened it), and abraytu the she-camel: I put a bura in her nose, which is a ring of iron; if it is of wood it is a khishāsh, and if it is of hair it is a khizāma. The pause form is «براءه» with hāʾ. Sībawayh said: They wanted to distinguish between this tāʾ and the tāʾ that is part of the root itself, like the tāʾ of «القت» [Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps al-qatt, "clover", is meant]. He said: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb claimed that some Arabs say «طلحت» [i.e. pausing with tāʾ], as they do with the tāʾ of the plural.
(مِنَ اللَّهِ): the nūn takes fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; this is the eloquent usage, and the grammarians hold several views about it. Al-Kisāʾī said: The original form of (من) is «منا»; they dropped the alif and kept the fatḥa. It is also said: they disliked combining two kasras, so in most places they gave it fatḥa. Abū Jaʿfar said: The best that has been said about this is the view of Sībawayh. He said: Since they used it so frequently, and it was not a verb, and fatḥa was lighter for them, they gave it fatḥa and likened it to «أين» and «كيف». Sībawayh said: Some Arabs give it kasra and say «من الله» [min-i llāh], according to analogy. Abū Ḥātim said: Hārūn claimed that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read «براءة من الله إلى الذين عاهدتم» [Translator's note: presumably with kasra, min-i llāh; the vowelling is not shown in the source]. If you wish you may say «عاهدتمو», according to the original form, or the elision, because the wāw is heavy.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: (فَإِخْوانُكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ): i.e. "then they are your brothers".

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: (فَقاتِلُوا أَئِمَّةَ الْكُفْرِ): plural of «إمام». The original form is «أأممة», like «مثال» and «أمثلة»; then the mīm was assimilated into the mīm, and the vowel was shifted onto the hamza, [giving] two hamzas, so the second was replaced by a yāʾ. Al-Akhfash claimed that you say «هذا أيمّ من هذا» ("this one is more fit to lead than this one"), with yāʾ. Al-Māzinī said: «أومّ», with wāw. Ḥamza read «فقاتلوا أامّة الكفر» [Translator's note: i.e. aʾimmata with two realised hamzas]. Most grammarians hold that this is an error (laḥn) that is not permissible, because it combines two hamzas in one word. Abū Isḥāq claimed that it is permissible though far-fetched. He said: Because two processes have occurred in the word, assimilation and doubling; so when the vowel of the mīm was cast onto the hamza, the hamza was left so that its vowel indicates that.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: (أَلا تُقاتِلُونَ): a rebuke, and it contains the sense of urging (taḥḍīḍ).

nahhas-irab:14-15.t:
(قاتِلُوهُمْ): an imperative. (يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ): its answer, and it is jussive (majzūm) in the sense of requital (mujāzāt); the implied form is "if you fight them, Allah will punish them". (بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَيُخْزِهِمْ وَيَنْصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُؤْمِنِينَ).
(وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ): all of it is conjoined. In all of it the nominative is permissible, as a break (qaṭʿ) from the first, and the accusative is permissible by an implied «أن», construed according to the meaning; the Kufans call it "by ṣarf (deflection)", as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 179-
فإن يهلك أبو قابوس يهلك ... ربيع النّاس والشّهر الحرام
ونأخذ بعده بذناب عيش ... أجبّ الظّهر ليس له سنام
("If Abū Qābūs perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred month perish; and after him we shall hold on to the tail-end of a life, like a camel with a cut-off back that has no hump.")
If you wish you make «ونأخذ» nominative, and if you wish you make it accusative. (وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ): the reading is with the nominative, because it is not of the same kind as the first: fighting does not entail for them repentance from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, whereas it does entail for them punishment, disgrace, the healing of the believers' breasts and the removal of the rage of their hearts. Comparable to it is (فَإِنْ يَشَإِ اللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلى قَلْبِكَ): the sentence is complete; then He said (وَيَمْحُ اللَّهُ الْباطِلَ) [al-Shūrā: 24]. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «ويتوب الله» in the accusative, and the same is reported from ʿĪsā and al-Aʿraj. (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: (أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ): a transition from one thing to another. (أَنْ تُتْرَكُوا): in the position of the two objects according to Sībawayh's view; according to Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad], the second has been omitted. (وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ): jussive by «لمّا»; even though «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), according to Sībawayh it serves as an answer to your saying "it has been done" (qad faʿala); the mīm is given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Farrāʾ said: (وَلِيجَةً) means intimates from among the polytheists whom they take, to whom they divulge their secrets and whom they inform of their affairs.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: (أَنْ يَعْمُرُوا مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ): the ism of kāna. (شاهِدِينَ): as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وأُولئِكَ): mubtadaʾ (subject); (حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ): the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: (إِنَّما يَعْمُرُ مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ): (ما) is restrictive (kāffa), and the verb comes first because it belongs to «من». (وَلَمْ يَخْشَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ): the alif is dropped for the jussive. Sībawayh said: Know that when the final letter is quiescent in the nominative, it is dropped in the jussive, so that the jussive is not the same as the nominative. (فَعَسى أُولئِكَ أَنْ يَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُهْتَدِينَ): «عسى» from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, denotes certainty.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: (أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقايَةَ الْحاجِّ): the implied form in Arabic is "have you made the people of the watering of the pilgrims …". It is also said: the implied form is "like the faith of one who believed in Allah", the noun being put in the place of the maṣdar since its meaning is known, like «إنّما السخاء حاتم» ("generosity is Ḥātim") and «إنّما الشعر زهير» ("poetry is Zuhayr"). (وَعِمارَةَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ) is like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]. Abū Wajza read «أجعلتم سقاة الحاجّ وعمرة المسجد الحرام». «سقاة» is the plural of «ساق»; its original form is «سقية» on the pattern fuʿala, and so is the plural of the weak verbs of this kind, such as «قاض» and «قضاة», and «ناس» and «نساة». If it is not weak, it takes the plural on the pattern faʿala, like «ناسئ» and «نسأة», for those who used to postpone the months.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: (فَسِيحُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ): al-Kisāʾī said: the maṣdar (verbal noun) is suyūḥ, sayaḥān and siyāḥa. Al-Farrāʾ said: and the water flowed (sāḥa), sayḥan. (أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ): the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] is kept to distinguish masculine from feminine. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned it, and mentioned what these months are. (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ): in the position of the accusative by «اعلموا»; and if you wish you may say «أنّكمو», as has been explained. «غير معجزي الله»: the nūn is dropped for the iḍāfa (genitive construct). According to Sībawayh's view it is also permissible to drop it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters and to put [the following noun] in the accusative.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ). (ودَرَجَةً) is by way of clarification (bayān) [Translator's note: i.e. a tamyīz (specification)].

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا آباءَكُمْ وَإِخْوانَكُمْ أَوْلِياءَ): two objects. (إِنِ اسْتَحَبُّوا الْكُفْرَ عَلَى الْإِيمانِ): i.e. do not obey them and do not take them as your confidants.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
(قُلْ إِنْ كانَ آباؤُكُمْ): the ism of «كان», and what follows is conjoined to it. (أَحَبَّ إِلَيْكُمْ): the khabar of kāna. Outside the Qur'an it would be permissible to put «أحبّ» in the nominative, as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), with the ism of kāna latent in it. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 180-
إذا متّ كان النّاس صنفان شامت ... وآخر مثن بالّذي كنت أصنع
("When I die, people will be of two kinds: one gloating, and another praising what I used to do.")
And Sībawayh recited: [al-Basīṭ] 181-
هي الشّفاء لدائي لو ظفرت بها ... وليس منها شفاء الدّاء مبذول
("She is the cure for my ailment, if only I could win her; but the cure of the ailment is not given freely by her.")

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
(لَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي مَواطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ): al-Farrāʾ said: «مواطن» is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) because it is a plural that has no counterpart among singulars and has no plural of its own, except that a poet may be compelled and pluralise it; and what is permissible in poetry is not found in [ordinary] speech. He recited: [al-Rajaz] 182-
فهنّ يعلكن حدائداتها
("And they champ on their iron bits.")
Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq marvelling at this. He said: He took the view of al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, and got it wrong, because al-Khalīl says it is a diptote because it is a plural that has no counterpart in the singular and does not take a broken plural; as for [a plural] with alif and tāʾ, that is not ruled out.
(وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ): an adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. "and He helped you on the day of Ḥunayn". «حنين» is fully declinable because it is masculine, the name of a valley; some Arabs do not decline it, making it the name of a place (buqʿa). (فَلَمْ تُغْنِ عَنْكُمْ): the yāʾ is dropped for the jussive.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: (ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): i.e. He sent down upon them what calmed them and removed their fear, until they dared to fight the polytheists. (وَأَنْزَلَ جُنُوداً لَمْ تَرَوْها): they are the angels, who strengthen the believers with the thoughts and steadfastness they cast into their hearts, and weaken the disbelievers by making them cowardly, without their seeing them and without fighting, because the angels, the blessings of Allah be upon them, did not fight except on the day of Badr.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: (إِنَّمَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (فَلا يَقْرَبُوا): a prohibition; that is why the nūn is dropped from it.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: (وَأَذانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ): conjoined to «براءة». (يَوْمَ الْحَجِّ الْأَكْبَرِ): an adverbial (ẓarf); we have mentioned what was said about it. The lesser ḥajj is the ʿumra. (أَنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): in the position of the accusative, the implied form being «بأن الله» ("that Allah …"). Whoever reads «إنّ الله» takes it to mean "He said: Indeed Allah …". (بَرِيءٌ): khabar (predicate). (وَرَسُولِهِ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading being discussed is wa-rasūluhu, nominative]: conjoined to the position [of the ism of anna], or, if you wish, to the latent pronoun; both are good because the sentence has become long. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (أَنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَرَسُولُهُ) [Translator's note: the source prints wa-rasūluhu, but the reading attributed to these two is otherwise reported as wa-rasūlahu in the accusative, which fits "conjoined to the wording"], conjoined to the wording.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
(وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ وَقالَتِ النَّصارى الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ ذلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ يُضاهِؤُنَ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ) (30)
(وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ): the grammarians hold several views about this. Among the best of them is that it is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being "our master is ʿUzayr, [son …]". Al-Akhfash recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 183-
لعمرك ما أدري وإن كنت داريا ... شعيب بن سهم أم شعيب بن منقر
("By your life, I do not know — though I am one who knows — whether it is Shuʿayb ibn Sahm or Shuʿayb ibn Minqar.")
It is also permissible for (عُزَيْرٌ) to be nominative as a mubtadaʾ with (ابْنُ) as its khabar (predicate), the tanwīn being dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; Sībawayh permitted exactly this. A third view is that of Abū Ḥātim. He said: If someone were to say that «عزير» is a non-Arabic name, and that is why the tanwīn was dropped from it… Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is wrong, because «عزير» is an Arabic name, derived [from the root ʿ-z-r]; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said (وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ) [al-Fatḥ: 9]. And even if it were non-Arabic it would be declinable, because it originally has three letters, and then the yāʾ of the diminutive was added to it. The leading readers in reading and language have read (عُزَيْرٌ) with tanwīn: Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Abān ibn Taghlib, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read (وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ), and this is clear as mubtadaʾ and khabar; likewise (وَقالَتِ النَّصارى الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ), and likewise (ذلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ).
ʿĀṣim and Ṭalḥa read (يُضاهِؤُنَ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا), taking the hamza as radical and positing «ضهيئا» on the pattern faʿīl. Omitting the hamza is better, because we know of no lexicographer who reported that faʿīl exists in the language [Translator's note: so in the source; what is meant is presumably faʿīʾ/faʿyal for ḍahyaʾ, the pattern being uncertain in the printed text]. If it is not read with hamza, one posits «ظهياء» [Translator's note: so in the source, with ẓāʾ; presumably «ضهياء»] on the pattern faʿlāʾ, the hamza being additional, as it is added in «شأمل» and «غرقئ»; except that it is possible that it is faʿīl without a counterpart, just as «كنهبل» is a faʿalla pattern without a counterpart [Translator's note: the source writes «فنعلل»] and «قرنفل» is a faʿalla pattern without a counterpart [Translator's note: the source writes «فعنلل»].

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: (اتَّخَذُوا أَحْبارَهُمْ وَرُهْبانَهُمْ أَرْباباً مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): two objects. (وَالْمَسِيحَ ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): accusative by an implied verb; it may also be conjoined.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t:
(يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ): He made the proofs equivalent to light because of the clarity they contain.
(بِأَفْواهِهِمْ): plural of «فوه», according to the original form, because the original of «فم» is «فوه», like «حوض» and «أحواض». (وَيَأْبَى اللَّهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ): it may be asked: how does «إلّا» come in when there is no particle of negation in the sentence? For one cannot say «ضربت إلّا زيدا» ("I struck except Zayd"). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «إلّا» came into the sentence only as a fringe (ṭaraf) of negation. Abū Isḥāq said: Negation and affirmation do not have fringes; the instruments of negation are «ما ولا ولم ولن وليس», and these have no fringes that are pronounced. If the matter were as he intended, «كرهت إلا زيدا» ("I disliked except Zayd") would be permissible. Rather, the answer is that the Arabs make an omission with «أبى», the implied form being "and Allah refuses everything except to perfect His light".
ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: He permitted this only with «يأبى» because it denotes prevention or refusal, so it resembled negation. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 184-
وهل لي أمّ غيرها إن تركتها ... أبى الله إلّا أن أكون لها ابنما
("Have I any mother other than her, if I were to leave her? Allah refuses anything but that I be a son to her.")

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (لِيُظْهِرَهُ): the lām of kay (purpose), i.e. to make it prevail by argument and proofs; and He has made it prevail.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
(إِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ الْأَحْبارِ وَالرُّهْبانِ لَيَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوالَ النَّاسِ): the lām comes in on yafʿalu (the imperfect) but not on faʿala (the past), because yafʿalu resembles nouns. (وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ): nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it may also be conjoined to what is in «يأكلون», i.e. "and those who hoard gold and silver consume it". (وَلا يُنْفِقُونَها فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): He did not say «ينفقونهما» (them both); there are four views on this. The implied form may be "and they do not spend the treasures"; or "and they do not spend the wealth"; or "and they do not spend the silver", with omission from the first because the second indicates it — and Sībawayh recited: [al-Munsariḥ] 185-
نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما عندك ... راض والرّأي مختلف
("We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content — though opinion differs.")
— and the fourth implied form is that «ينفقونها» refers to the gold, with the second conjoined to it. (فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): in the position of the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, i.e. put a painful punishment for them in the place of good tidings.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: (يَوْمَ): an adverbial (ẓarf); the implied form is "they will be punished [on the day]". (يَوْمَ يُحْمى عَلَيْها فِي نارِ جَهَنَّمَ). (فَتُكْوى بِها جِباهُهُمْ): the noun of a verb whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. (وَجُنُوبُهُمْ وَظُهُورُهُمْ): conjoined. (هذا ما كَنَزْتُمْ): i.e. it will be said to them.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
(إِنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ اثْنا عَشَرَ شَهْراً): the ism of «إنّ» and its khabar. (اثْنا عَشَرَ) is declined, unlike its counterparts, because it contains the letter of declension or its indicator. (ذلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: (ذلِكَ الدِّينُ), i.e. "that is the decree". (فَلا تَظْلِمُوا فِيهِنَّ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): it is more likely that this refers to the four [sacred months], because what the Arabs mostly use for what exceeds ten is «فيها ومنها» [i.e. the feminine singular pronoun rather than «فيهنّ»]. (وَقاتِلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ كَافَّةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq said: Like this among maṣdars are «عافاه الله عافية» and «عاقبه عاقبة»; it is neither dualised nor pluralised, and likewise «عامّة» and «خاصّة».
He said: The meaning of «كافة» is "encompassing them"; it is derived from the kuffa of a thing, which is its edge, because when you reach it you refrain (kafafta) from going further.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
(إِنَّمَا النَّسِيءُ زِيادَةٌ فِي الْكُفْرِ): this is how most of the leading readers read it, and no one, as far as we know, has related from Nāfiʿ (إِنَّمَا النَّسِيءُ) without hamza except Warsh alone. It is derived from nasaʾahu and ansaʾahu, when he postponed it; al-Kisāʾī reported both usages. So nasīʾ means mansūʾ or munsaʾ (postponed). Abū ʿUbayd said: Ibn Kathīr read it without lengthening and without hamza. Abū Ḥātim said: Ibn Kathīr read it with a sukūn on the sīn. Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known of Ibn Kathīr's reading is (إِنَّمَا النَّسِيءُ زِيادَةٌ فِي الْكُفْرِ) on the pattern faʿīl.
The people of the two Sanctuaries and Abū ʿAmr read (يُضَلُّ بِهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا), the Kufans read (يُضَلُّ بِهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا), and al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read (يُضَلُّ بِهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḍād [Translator's note: the source prints all three readings with the same vowelling; the commonly reported readings are yaḍillu for the Ḥijāzīs and Abū ʿAmr, yuḍallu for the Kufans, and yuḍillu for al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ]. Each of the three readings conveys a meaning, and the Prophet ﷺ said: «أوتيت جوامع الكلم» ("I have been given comprehensive words"). «فيضلّ به الذين كفروا» [i.e. yaḍillu]: except that they reckon it, and so they go astray by it; «ويضلّ به الذين كفروا» [i.e. yuḍallu] in the sense of what is reckoned for them; and (يُضَلُّ بِهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) [i.e. yuḍillu], with its object omitted, i.e. "those who disbelieve lead astray by it whoever accepts it from them". (لِيُواطِؤُا): accusative by the lām of kay (purpose); (فَيُحِلُّوا) is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (ما لَكُمْ إِذا قِيلَ لَكُمُ انْفِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ اثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ): the original is «تثاقلتم»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the thāʾ because of its closeness to it, so you needed the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) to reach the pronunciation of the quiescent letter. The meaning is: you clung heavily to the comforts of the earth and to staying on the earth; and the implied sense is: "are you content with the comforts of this world instead of the comforts of the Hereafter?" (فَما مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (إِلَّا تَنْفِرُوا): a condition, which is why the nūn is dropped from it, and the answer is (يُعَذِّبْكُمْ). (وَيَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْماً غَيْرَكُمْ وَلا تَضُرُّوهُ شَيْئاً): conjoined. (وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:4-5.t:
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): in the position of the accusative by exception.
Al-Akhfash said: The implied form is «واقعدوا لهم على كل مرصد» ("and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush"), and «على» was dropped. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh reported «ضرب الظهر والبطن» ("he struck the back and the belly"), with «على» dropped; except that (كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ) being made accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf) is good, as you say: [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here; the example is missing.]

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
(إِلَّا تَنْصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ): protasis and apodosis (sharṭ wa-mujāzāt). (إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): an adverbial (ẓarf).
(ثانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they drove him out alone, apart from all people except Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him; i.e. "one of two". ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: The implied form is "so he went out the second of two", like (وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً) [Nūḥ: 17]. (إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصاحِبِهِ لا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنا): so He, Majestic and Mighty, extolled the mention of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and raised his rank through his going out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his sacrificing of himself; had he wished to emigrate in safety, he would have done so. His words (لا تَحْزَنْ) carry the sense of granting him safety, as He said (لا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعْلى) [Ṭāhā: 68], and said in the story of Lūṭ, peace be upon him, (لا تَخَفْ وَلا تَحْزَنْ) [al-ʿAnkabūt: 33], and in the story of Ibrāhīm ﷺ (لا تَخَفْ) [al-Dhāriyāt: 28]. And he said (إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنا), i.e. He helps us and protects us; so by this He affirmed for Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, piety and excellence, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said (إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ) [al-Naḥl: 128].
(فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ): the view of most of the exegetes and lexicographers is that the meaning is "so Allah sent down His tranquillity upon Abū Bakr", because the Prophet ﷺ already knew that he was protected, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, had commanded him to go out and [promised] that He would save him. The evidence for this is that he said to Abū Bakr (لا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنا), and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, calmed down; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said «فأنزل الله سكينته عليه». The meaning of the fāʾ in Arabic is that the second follows the first; so when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him «لا تحزن إنّ الله معنا», he calmed down and was reassured [Translator's note: the source reads «فكما قال لرسول الله», literally "when he said to the Messenger of Allah"; the sense requires "when the Messenger of Allah said to him"]. This is not like (فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) [al-Fatḥ: 26], because that was on the day of Ḥunayn: when the Muslims were thrown into disarray, the Prophet ﷺ feared [for them], though he knew that he himself was protected; and when Allah strengthened the believers and they returned, the Prophet ﷺ calmed down at that, and the fear that had come over him for the believers left him [Translator's note: the verse quoted is al-Tawba: 26; the source's reference «[الفتح: 26]» is to a similarly worded verse].
(وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَمْ تَرَوْها): the hāʾ refers back to the Prophet ﷺ, so the two pronouns refer to different persons. This is frequent in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said (أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كانَ عَلَى الْهُدى أَوْ أَمَرَ بِالتَّقْوى أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى) [al-ʿAlaq: 11, 12, 13], then said (أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرى) [al-ʿAlaq: 14].
(وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلى): i.e. He described it thus. (وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (هِيَ الْعُلْيا): mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), and the mubtadaʾ and khabar together are the khabar of the first. It is also possible for «العليا» to be the khabar and «هي» a separating pronoun (fāṣila). Al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb read (وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ) [i.e. kalimata] in the accusative, conjoined to the first. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that this is unlikely. He said: Because you say «أعتق فلان غلام أبيه» ("so-and-so freed his father's slave"), but you do not say «غلام أبي فلان» ("the slave of so-and-so's father", repeating the name). Abū Ḥātim said something similar; he said: it would then be «وكلمته هي العليا» ("and His word is the highest"). Abū Jaʿfar said: What al-Farrāʾ mentioned [Translator's note: the source has «الفقراء», evidently a misprint for «الفراء»] does not resemble the verse; rather, what resembles it is what Sībawayh recited: [al-Khafīf] 186-
لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء ... نغّص الموت ذا الغنى والفقيرا
("I see nothing outrun death; death has marred the life of the rich man and the poor.")
This is good and fine, because there is no difficulty in it; rather, the skilled grammarians say that repeating the noun in a case like this has a benefit, namely that it carries a sense of magnification. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said (إِذا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزالَها وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقالَها) [al-Zalzala: 1, 2], and there is no difficulty in this. (وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
(وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ اسْتَجارَكَ): i.e. [seeks your protection] from being killed. (وأَحَدٌ) is nominative by an implied verb like the one after it; this is good after «إن» and ugly after its sisters. Sībawayh's position on the difference between «إن» and its sisters is that, since it is the mother of the conditional particles — because it is used for nothing else — it was singled out for this. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: As for his saying "because it is used for nothing else", that is a mistake, because it can mean «ما» (not), can be redundant (zāʾida), and can be lightened from the heavy [inna]; rather, it is vague, and the others are not like that. Sībawayh recited: [al-Kāmil] 177-
لا تجزعي إن منفسا أهلكته ... وإذا هلكت فعند ذلك فاجزعي
("Do not grieve if I have spent something precious; but when I perish, then grieve.")
(ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُ): two objects, the preposition having been dropped from one of them. The plural [of «مأمن»] is «مآمن».

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (كَيْفَ يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ عَهْدٌ): the ism of «يكون». (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتُمْ): exception. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: They are Banū Bakr.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
(كَيْفَ وَإِنْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ): al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: Something is implied, i.e. "how could you not kill them?" — and Allah knows best. Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is "how can they have a covenant?", then it was omitted, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 178-
وخبرتماني أنّما الموت بالقرى ... فكيف وهذا هضبة وكثيب
("You two told me that death is only in the towns — so how, when here are a hill and a sand-dune?")
He said: The implied form is "and how did he die?". (لا يَرْقُبُوا فِيكُمْ إِلًّا وَلا ذِمَّةً), and after it (لا يَرْقُبُونَ فِي مُؤْمِنٍ إِلًّا وَلا ذِمَّةً): this is not repetition; rather, the first is about all the polytheists and the second about the Jews specifically. The evidence for this is His words (اشْتَرَوْا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلًا), meaning the Jews: they sold the proofs of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and His clear explanation, seeking leadership and out of greed for something. The plural of «إل» is «آلال» for a small number, and for a large number «ألال»; and «ذمّة», plural «ذمم».

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: (انْفِرُوا): al-Akhfash reported «انفروا» [Translator's note: presumably the variant with ḍamma, unfurū; the vowelling is not shown in the source]. (خِفافاً وَثِقالًا): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). There are two views about it: one is that it is abrogated by His words (فَلَوْلا نَفَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ مِنْهُمْ طائِفَةٌ) [al-Tawba: 122]; the other is that it is not abrogated, because jihad is an obligation, except that some Muslims discharge it on behalf of others; but when necessity arises, jihad becomes obligatory on everyone.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (لَوْ كانَ عَرَضاً قَرِيباً): the khabar (predicate) of kāna. (وَسَفَراً قاصِداً): conjoined to it. (لَاتَّبَعُوكَ): this pronoun refers to the hypocrites, because they are included among those addressed with the call to march out. This is found in the speech of the Arabs: they mention the whole group and then bring a pronoun referring back to part of it, as was said about the words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, (وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها) [Maryam: 71], that it is the Resurrection; then He, Majestic and Mighty, said (ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيها جِثِيًّا) [Maryam: 72], meaning — Majestic and Mighty is He — Hell. Abū ʿUbayda reported that (الشُّقَّةُ) is the journey, and al-Kisāʾī reported that one says shuqqa and shiqqa.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
(عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْكَ): there are two views about its meaning. One is that it is an opening of speech, as you say "may Allah set you right, such-and-such happened". The other view — and it is more fitting — is that the meaning is "Allah has pardoned you whatever fault there was in your giving them permission". This is indicated by (لِمَ أَذِنْتَ لَهُمْ), because one does not say "why did you do what I commanded you?"
The original [of «لم»] is «لما»; the alif was dropped to distinguish the interrogative from the declarative, and because «ما» has become attached to the lām. One cannot pause on it except with hāʾ: «لمه».

nahhas-irab:44-45.t: (لا يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ أَنْ يُجاهِدُوا): in the position of the accusative. Abū Isḥāq said: The implied form is "about striving" (fī an yujāhidū). Someone else said: This is a mistake; rather, the meaning is the opposite of this, and the implied form is (إِنَّما يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ) to stay behind, so as not to strive; and its literal sense in Arabic is "out of dislike that they should not strive", as He, Majestic and Mighty, said (يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا) [al-Nisāʾ: 76] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Nisāʾ: 176].

nahhas-irab:46-47.t:
(وَلكِنْ كَرِهَ اللَّهُ انْبِعاثَهُمْ): because they said: "If we are given permission to stay at home [that is that]; [otherwise] we will cause corruption and stir up trouble against the Muslims." This is indicated by what comes after it: (لَوْ خَرَجُوا فِيكُمْ ما زادُوكُمْ إِلَّا خَبالًا). (فَثَبَّطَهُمْ): i.e. Allah, Majestic and Mighty. (وَقِيلَ اقْعُدُوا مَعَ الْقاعِدِينَ): the implied form may be "the Prophet ﷺ said to them", and this would be the permission mentioned earlier; it is also said: the meaning is "their companions said this to them".
(يَبْغُونَكُمُ الْفِتْنَةَ): a second object. The meaning is: they seek sedition for you, i.e. corruption and incitement. One says baghaytuhu such-and-such, i.e. I helped him seek it, and baghaytuhu such-and-such, I sought it for him.
(لَقَدِ ابْتَغَوُا الْفِتْنَةَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَقَلَّبُوا لَكَ الْأُمُورَ حَتَّى جاءَ الْحَقُّ وَظَهَرَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَهُمْ كارِهُونَ) (48). (لَقَدِ ابْتَغَوُا الْفِتْنَةَ مِنْ قَبْلُ): i.e. they had sought corruption before their affair was exposed and revelation came down about what they concealed and what they would do; for He, Majestic and Mighty, said (سَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَكُمْ) [Barāʾa: 95], informing of their fault. «وقلّبوا لك الأمور»: i.e. they schemed and contrived to sow discord and corruption.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t:
(وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ ائْذَنْ لِي): from adhina, yaʾdhanu. When you form the imperative you add a hamza with kasra, preceded by [Translator's note: so in the source; "followed by" is meant] a hamza that is the first radical of the verb; two hamzas do not combine, so the second is replaced by a yāʾ because of the kasra before it, and you say «ائذن لي» (īdhan lī). When you join it [to what precedes], the reason for avoiding two hamzas disappears, so you pronounce the hamza and say «ومنهم من يقول أذن لي» [i.e. … yaqūlu ʾdhan lī]. Warsh related from Nāfiʿ «ومنهم من يقول اذن لي», lightening the hamza.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says «ائذن لفلان ثم ائذن لفلان» ("give permission to so-and-so, then give permission to so-and-so"), and the spelling of the first and the second is the same, with an alif and a yāʾ before the dhāl in writing. But if you say «ائذن لفلان وأذن لغيره» ("… and give permission to someone else"), the second is without yāʾ; and likewise with fāʾ. The difference between «ثم» on the one hand and the fāʾ and the wāw on the other is that one may pause on «ثم» and it stands separately, whereas one does not pause on the fāʾ and the wāw, and they do not stand separately.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: (إِنْ تُصِبْكَ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ): protasis and apodosis (sharṭ wa-mujāzāt), and likewise (وَإِنْ تُصِبْكَ مُصِيبَةٌ يَقُولُوا قَدْ أَخَذْنا أَمْرَنا مِنْ قَبْلُ). (وَيَتَوَلَّوْا): conjoined.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: (قُلْ لَنْ يُصِيبَنا): accusative (subjunctive) by «لن». Abū ʿUbayda reported that some Arabs put the jussive after it. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «هل يصيبنا», and it is related that Aʿyan, the judge of al-Rayy, read «قل لن يصبّنا» with a doubled nūn; this is an error (laḥn): what is a statement is not emphasised with the nūn. Had this been in Ṭalḥa's reading [i.e. with «هل»], it would be permissible; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said (هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ ما يَغِيظُ) [al-Ḥajj: 15]. (ما كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنا): «ما» is in the position of the nominative. (هُوَ مَوْلانا): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): jussive because it is a command; the second lām is given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. If you wish you may give the first [lām] kasra according to the original, and the sukūn is because of the heaviness of the kasra.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: (قُلْ هَلْ تَرَبَّصُونَ بِنا): the Kufans assimilate the lām into the tāʾ. As for the lām of the definite article, nothing but assimilation is permissible with it, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said (التَّائِبُونَ) [al-Tawba: 112], because the lām of the definite article is so frequent in their speech. Assimilation is not permissible in His words (قُلْ تَعالَوْا) [al-Anʿām: 151], because «قل» is a weak verb, and they would be combining two processes on it. The singular of (الْحُسْنَيَيْنِ) is «الحسنى», and the plural is «الحسن»; it may only be uttered with the definite article: one does not say «رأيت امرأة حسنى». (وَنَحْنُ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمْ أَنْ يُصِيبَكُمُ اللَّهُ): in the position of the accusative by «نتربّص».

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
(قُلْ أَنْفِقُوا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The wording of «أنفقوا» is that of a command, but its meaning is condition and requital. This is how the Arabs use it in cases like this: they bring «أو», as [the poet said]: [al-Ṭawīl] 187-
أسيئي بنا أو أحسني لا ملومة ... لدينا ولا مقليّة إن تقلّت
("Treat us ill or treat us well — you are not blamed by us, nor hated, even if you turn hateful.")
The meaning is: whether you treat us ill or well, we are for you as you know. The meaning of the verse is: whether you spend willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. Then He, Majestic and Mighty, explained why it would not be accepted from them, and said: [Translator's note: the quotation continues in the following verse, 9:54.]

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: (أَنْ): the first is in the position of the accusative and the second in the position of the nominative. The meaning is: "nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except their disbelief". The Kufans read «أن يقبل منهم نفقاتهم» [with the masculine yāʾ], because «النفقات» and «الإنفاق» are one and the same. Abū Isḥāq said: It is permissible [to read] «وما منعهم أن يقبل منهم نفقاتهم» (إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ) [i.e. yaqbala, active], meaning "nothing prevented Allah from accepting their expenditures (إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا)"; then the first and the second are in the position of the accusative. According to Sībawayh, it is permissible for them to be in the position of the genitive.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
(لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأً): this is how one pauses on it, and in writing it has two alifs: the first is the hamza and the second is a substitute for the tanwīn; likewise «رأيت جزأا». (أَوْ مَغاراتٍ): from ghāra, yaghīru. Al-Akhfash said: (مَغاراتٍ) is also possible from aghāra, yughīru [i.e. mughārāt], as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 188-
الحمد لله ممسانا ومصبحنا ... بالخير صبّحنا ربّي ومسّانا
("Praise be to Allah in our evening and our morning; with good my Lord has brought us morning and evening.")
(أَوْ مُدَّخَلًا): there are five readings of it. This is one of them. It is related from Qatāda, ʿĪsā and al-Aʿmash: (أَوْ مُدَّخَلًا) with doubling of the dāl and the khāʾ [i.e. muddakhkhalan]. In the text of Ubayy: «أو متدخّلا». Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «أو مدخلا» with fatḥa on the mīm and sukūn on the dāl [madkhalan]. Abū Isḥāq said: It is also read «أو مدخلا» with ḍamma on the mīm and sukūn on the dāl [mudkhalan]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The original of «مدّخل» is «مدتخل»; the tāʾ was changed into dāl because the dāl is voiced (majhūra) and the tāʾ voiceless (mahmūsa), and they share one point of articulation. The original of the first in «مدّخّل» is «مدتخّل»; it is also said that its original is «متدخّل» on the pattern mutafaʿʿal, as in the reading of Ubayy. Its meaning is entering after entering, i.e. people they could enter among. «مدخل» [madkhal] is from dakhala, and «مدخل» [mudkhal] is from adkhala; and so are the maṣdar, the noun of place and the noun of time, as Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 189-
مغار ابن همّام على حيّ خثعما
("The raid of Ibn Hammām upon the tribe of Khathʿam.")
(وَهُمْ يَجْمَحُونَ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: Al-Aʿraj read «ومنهم من يلمزك» with ḍamma on the mīm [yalmuzuka]; but most transitive verbs [of this kind] take yafʿilu, with kasra on the middle radical.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: (فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun). (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ said: «فريضة من الله» [in the nominative] is also permissible, meaning "that is an obligation from Allah".

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: (وَمِنْهُمُ الَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ النَّبِيَّ): (الَّذِينَ) is in the position of the nominative. (يُؤْذُونَ) has a hamza because it is from ādhā; if you wish, you lighten the hamza and replace it with a wāw. (وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ أُذُنٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise (قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ) according to the reading of al-Ḥasan [Translator's note: al-Ḥasan's reading is reported as udhunun khayrun, with tanwīn; the source does not show the vowelling]. The people of Kufa read (قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ), and they read (وَرَحْمَةٌ) in the genitive, conjoined to «خير»; and this, according to the experts in Arabic, [is weak] because it separates the two nouns, and that is ugly with genitives [Translator's note: the source sentence appears incomplete; the genitive raḥmatin is attributed to Ḥamza alone among the Kufans]. The nominative is by conjunction with «أذن», the implied form being "say: he is a hearer of good and he is a mercy", i.e. he is one who listens to what is good for you, i.e. one who listens to what ought to be listened to and accepts what ought to be accepted. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words, Majestic and Mighty, «ويقولون هو أذن»: he said: "a listener and a speaker". He said: (يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَيُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): he believes in Allah and believes the believers. Abū Jaʿfar said: On this [interpretation] the lām is redundant (zāʾida) according to the Kufans, and like it is (هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ) [al-Aʿrāf: 15] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Aʿrāf: 154]; according to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to a maṣdar indicated by the verb.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: (وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Sībawayh holds that the implied form is "Allah is more worthy that they should please Him, and His Messenger is more worthy that they should please him", and then [one of them] was omitted. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: There is no omission in the sentence; the implied form is "Allah — more worthy that they should please Him — and His Messenger", by way of fronting and postponing. Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is "[the Messenger] is more worthy that they should please him", and «والله» is an opening of speech, as you say "what Allah wills and you will". Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Sībawayh is the most fitting of them, because it is authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ that he forbade saying "what Allah wills and you will"; and no fronting or postponing is posited in anything [unnecessarily], while its meaning is sound.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t:
(أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا): the nūn is dropped for the jussive. (أَنَّهُ): in the position of the accusative by «يعلموا», and the hāʾ is a pronoun referring to the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). (مَنْ يُحادِدِ اللَّهَ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (فَأَنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ): it may be said: what follows the fāʾ in a condition is a mubtadaʾ, so it ought to have been «فإنّ له» with kasra on «إنّ». The grammarians hold four views about this. The position of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is that the second «أن» is a badal (substitute) for the first. Abū al-ʿAbbās claimed that this view is to be rejected and that what is correct is what al-Jarmī said; he said: the second [anna] is repeated for emphasis (tawkīd), and comparable to it is (وَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ) [al-Naml: 5], and likewise (فَكانَ عاقِبَتَهُما أَنَّهُما فِي النَّارِ خالِدَيْنِ فِيها) [al-Ḥashr: 17]. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is "then the necessity of the Fire is his". Abū al-ʿAbbās said: This statement of al-Akhfash is a mistake, because he begins with «أنّ» and implies the khabar (predicate). ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: The meaning is "then what is necessary is that he will have the fire of Hell". Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh permitted «فإنّ له نار جهنّم» with kasra. Sībawayh said: It is good; and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 190-
وعلمي بأسدام المياه فلم تزل ... قلائص تخدي في طريق طلائح
وأنّي إذا ملّت ركابي مناخها ... فإني على حظّي من الأمر جامح
("And my knowledge of the stagnant waters — for there were always young camels trotting, worn out, on the road — and that when my riding-camels tire of their resting place, I am headstrong in pursuit of my share of the matter.")

nahhas-irab:64-64.t:
(يَحْذَرُ الْمُنافِقُونَ): a statement (khabar), and what shows that it is one is that after it comes (إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْرِجٌ ما تَحْذَرُونَ), because they disbelieved out of obstinacy. It is also said: it has the sense of a command, as one says "let him do that" [using yafʿalu]. (أَنْ تُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُورَةٌ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. "of a sūra being sent down upon them". According to Sībawayh's view it may be in the position of the genitive, with «من» omitted; and it may be in the position of the accusative as an object, because Sībawayh permitted «حذرت زيدا» ("I was wary of Zayd"), and recited: [al-Kāmil] 191-
حذر أمورا لا تضير وآمن ... ما ليس منجيه من الأقدار
("Wary of things that do no harm, and feeling safe from what nothing will save him from among the decrees.")
According to Abū al-ʿAbbās this is one of the places where Sībawayh erred; in his view «أنا حذر زيدا» is not permissible, because ḥadhir is something in one's disposition and so is not transitive. Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān narrated to us; he said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī narrated to me; he said: al-Lāḥiqī said to me: Sībawayh met me and said to me, "Do you know [any evidence] for the governing power of the faʿil pattern?" I did not have anything memorised about that, [so I made up]: [al-Kāmil]
حذر أمورا لا تصير وآمن ... ما ليس منجيه من الأقدار
[Translator's note: the source text appears to break off here; the anecdote is usually given as al-Lāḥiqī confessing that he fabricated this verse for Sībawayh. The source prints «تصير» here and «تضير» above.]

nahhas-irab:65-66.t:
(وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّما كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلْعَبُ): then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that they had disbelieved, and said: (لا تَعْتَذِرُوا), i.e. do not make excuses by saying "we were only chatting and playing". (قُلْ أَبِاللَّهِ وَآياتِهِ وَرَسُولِهِ كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ); then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: (قَدْ كَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمانِكُمْ). (إِنْ نَعْفُ): the alif [i.e. the final weak letter] is dropped for the jussive. Al-Kisāʾī said: Zayd ibn Thābit read (إِنْ نَعْفُ عَنْ طائِفَةٍ مِنْكُمْ نُعَذِّبْ طائِفَةً) with the nūn, and «طائفة» in the accusative by «نعذّب»; and so read Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿĀṣim. Al-Jaḥdarī read «إن يعف عن طائفة» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the fāʾ, «يعذّب» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the dhāl, (طائِفَةٍ) [i.e. ṭāʾifatan] accusative by the verb. The meaning is: if He pardons a party that has repented, He will punish a party that has not repented. The lexicographers, among them al-Farrāʾ, reported that a single person is called «طائفة», and that one says «أكلت طائفة من الشّاة», i.e. a piece [of the sheep].
Abū Isḥāq said: It is related that these two parties were three [men]: two mocked and one laughed; so «طائفة» is used for one person, as one says «جاءتني طائفة», i.e. one man; and its implied form in Arabic is «جاءتني نفس طائفة» ("a single soul came to me").

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: (الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالْمُنافِقاتُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (بَعْضُهُمْ): a second mubtadaʾ; it may also be a badal (substitute), the khabar (predicate) being «من بعض». Abū Isḥāq said: This is connected with His words (وَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُمْ لَمِنْكُمْ وَما هُمْ مِنْكُمْ) [al-Tawba: 56], i.e. they are not of the believers, but they are of one another, i.e. alike in enjoining wrong, forbidding right, and withholding their hands from jihad.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: (خالِدِينَ): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (هِيَ حَسْبُهُمْ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: (كَالَّذِينَ): Abū Isḥāq said: The kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. Allah has promised the disbelievers the fire of Hell with a promise like the one He promised to those before them. (كانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْكُمْ قُوَّةً): the khabar (predicate) of kāna; it is a diptote because it is an afʿal adjective, its original being «أشدد». That is, they were stronger than you in power, yet they were unable to ward off the punishment of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. (فَاسْتَمْتَعُوا بِخَلاقِهِمْ): i.e. they benefited from their share of this world, as those before them did.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: (أَلَمْ يَأْتِهِمْ): the yāʾ is dropped for the jussive. (نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): nominative by «يأتي». (قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعادٍ وَثَمُودَ): a badal (substitute). Whoever does not decline «ثمود» makes it the name of the tribe. (وَالْمُؤْتَفِكاتِ): it is said that the people of Lūṭ are meant, because their land was overturned with them (iʾtafakat), i.e. turned upside down. It is also said: «المؤتفكات» is everyone who was destroyed, as one says "the world was overturned upon him".

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: (وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها وَمَساكِنَ طَيِّبَةً فِي جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ وَرِضْوانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ) (72). (وَرِضْوانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. greater than their [other] bliss. Outside the Qur'an the accusative would be permissible, because this is among the things they were promised.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: (جاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ وَالْمُنافِقِينَ): the dāl is given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the verb is not declinable (muʿrab). According to all the grammarians, the imperative verb can only be future, and likewise «سيفعل» and «سوف يفعل». As for «يفعل», the grammarians differ about it: the Basrans say it can be future and present; the Kufans say it is future, because these added letters were brought only as a sign of futurity. «فاعل» [the active participle] is, according to the Basrans, like «يفعل»; according to the Kufans it is for the present, unless it is figurative.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: (وَلَقَدْ قالُوا كَلِمَةَ الْكُفْرِ وَكَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِسْلامِهِمْ): this shows that the hypocrites are disbelievers, and in His words (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا) [al-Munāfiqūn: 3] there is decisive proof. (وَما نَقَمُوا إِلَّا أَنْ أَغْناهُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): (أن) is in the position of the accusative. (فَإِنْ يَتُوبُوا يَكُ خَيْراً لَهُمْ): protasis and apodosis (sharṭ wa-mujāzāt), and likewise (وَإِنْ يَتَوَلَّوْا يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ).

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ عاهَدَ اللَّهَ): in the position of the nominative.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: (فَأَعْقَبَهُمْ نِفاقاً): two objects. (إِلى يَوْمِ يَلْقَوْنَهُ): in the position of the genitive.

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: (الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The original is «المتطوّعين»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ. (وَالَّذِينَ لا يَجِدُونَ إِلَّا جُهْدَهُمْ): in the position of the genitive, conjoined to «المؤمنين». It cannot be conjoined to «المطّوّعين», because if you conjoined it to them you would be conjoining to the noun before it is complete, since (فَيَسْخَرُونَ) is conjoined to «يلمزون». (سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ): the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t:
(فَرِحَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلافَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); if you wish, it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
(قُلْ نارُ جَهَنَّمَ أَشَدُّ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (حَرًّا): by way of clarification (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)].

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: (فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلًا): a command carrying the sense of threat. The lām is originally with kasra, and the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness. (قَلِيلًا) and (كَثِيراً) are accusative as qualifiers of [an omitted] adverbial or maṣdar. (جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), for the requital.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: (وَلا تُصَلِّ عَلى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ): [the yāʾ] is dropped because it is jussive by «لا».

nahhas-irab:86-86.t: (وَإِذا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ أَنْ آمِنُوا): in the position of the accusative, i.e. «بأن آمنوا» ("that you believe").

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: (رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوالِفِ): plural of «خالفة», i.e. the women. A man may also be called «خالفة» and «خالف» when he is of no worth. However, fawāʿil is the plural of fāʿila, and fāʿil as an adjective is not pluralised as fawāʿil except in poetry, apart from two words, «فارس» and «هالك». As for «هالك», it is in a proverb; and as for «فارس», it gives rise to no ambiguity.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: (لكِنِ الرَّسُولُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ): conjoined to it. (جاهَدُوا بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ): in the position of the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: (وَجاءَ الْمُعَذِّرُونَ): al-Aʿraj and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read (الْمُعَذِّرُونَ) [Translator's note: i.e. al-muʿdhirūn, without doubling, as the following explanation shows; the source prints the doubled form]. This reading is related from Ibn ʿAbbās; the transmitters of readings related it, except that its chain revolves around al-Kalbī. It is from aʿdhara, when one goes to great lengths in excusing oneself. As for «المعذّرون» with doubling, there are two views about it. Al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ, Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd said: The original is «المعتذرون»; then it was assimilated and the vowel of the tāʾ was cast onto the ʿayn. According to them «المعذّرون» with ḍamma on the ʿayn is also permissible, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters and because what precedes is a ḍamma. And «المعذّرون» may [also] be those who make excuses while having no excuse. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: It cannot be [derived from] «المعتذرين», and assimilation is not permissible, as confusion would arise. Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq mentioned that assimilation is avoided according to the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, and that the context shows that they are blameworthy and have no excuse. He said: Because they came (لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ); had they been among the weak and the sick, or those who do not find anything to spend, they would not have needed to ask permission. Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of «المعذرة», «الإعذار» and «التعذير» is one thing, namely what is difficult and hard to achieve. The Arabs' saying «من عذير من فلان» means: he has done a grave thing for which he deserves that I punish him, and people do not know of it, so who will excuse me if I punish him? (لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ): accusative by the lām of kay (purpose).

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: (وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ مُنافِقُونَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. people who are hypocrites. We have mentioned that «المنافق» is derived from al-nāfiqāʾ [one of the burrow-holes of the jerboa]. In the ḥadīth: «المنافق الذي إذا حدّث كذّب وإذا وعد أخلف وإذا أؤتمن خان» ("The hypocrite is the one who, when he speaks, lies; when he promises, breaks it; and when he is entrusted, betrays"). (وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ مَرَدُوا عَلَى النِّفاقِ): your saying «مردوا» may be a naʿt (adjective) for «المنافقين», and the implied form may also be "and among the people of Medina are people who have persisted in hypocrisy".

nahhas-irab:103-103.t:
(خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِها): this is the obligatory zakāt, according to what has been related. There are five constructions for it. Abū Isḥāq said: The best is that the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. "for you purify them and cleanse them by it"; it may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Akhfash said: It may also refer to the charity [i.e. "a charity which purifies them"], and then (اتَّبَعُوهُمْ) is an emphasis (tawkīd) [Translator's note: so in the source; «اتبعوهم» does not belong here — presumably «وتزكيهم» is meant]. It is also possible that «تطهّرهم» refers to the charity and «تزكّيهم» to the Prophet ﷺ. The fifth construction is that it be jussive as the answer to the command, as Imruʾ al-Qays said: [al-Ṭawīl] 192-
قفا نبك من ذكرى حبيب وعرفان
("Halt, you two, and let us weep at the memory of a beloved and of a dwelling recognised.")
(وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ): there are two answers about it. One is that it is abrogated by His words, Majestic and Mighty, (وَلا تُصَلِّ عَلى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ ماتَ أَبَداً) [al-Tawba: 84]. The other is that it is not abrogated, and that the meaning is "and pray for them when they come to you with the charities"; this is what the Prophet ﷺ used to do, and the scholars hold this. It is indicated by (إِنَّ صَلاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ), i.e. when you pray for them as they come to you with their charities, that calms their hearts, and they rejoice and hasten, out of desire for the Prophet's ﷺ supplication. All the lexicographers, as far as we know, report that ṣalāt in the speech of the Arabs is supplication, and from it is the prayer over the deceased.

nahhas-irab:104-104.t: (أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبادِهِ): (أنّ) has fatḥa [because it is governed by] «يعلموا»; had there been a lām in its khabar (predicate), you would give it kasra. «هو» is a separating pronoun (fāṣila), or, if you wish, a mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:105-105.t: (وَقُلِ اعْمَلُوا فَسَيَرَى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ): this is from seeing with the eye and nothing else, because it takes only one object.

nahhas-irab:106-106.t: (وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ): conjoined; the implied form is "and among them are others deferred (murjaʾūn) for the command of Allah", from arjaʾtuhu, "I postponed it"; and from it the Murjiʾa are so called, because they postponed works. Whoever reads (مُرْجَوْنَ) has two possible analyses: one is that it is from arjaytuhu [Translator's note: the second analysis is not stated in the source as printed]. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: One does not say arjaytuhu in the sense of "I postponed it"; rather it would be from rajāʾ (hope). (إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ): «إما» in Arabic is for one of two things. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows the outcome of things, but the address is to the servants according to what they know, i.e. let their affair be, in your view, a matter of hope, because the servants have nothing more than this.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t:
(وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مَسْجِداً ضِراراً وَكُفْراً): conjoined, i.e. "and among them are those who took a mosque"; it may also be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Whoever reads (الَّذِينَ) without wāw — and it is the reading of the Medinans — takes it as nominative as a mubtadaʾ and nothing else. There are two views about the khabar (predicate). Al-Kisāʾī claimed that the implied form is "those who took a mosque — do not stand in it ever", i.e. do not stand in their mosque, as [the poet] said: [al-Sarīʿ] 193-
من باب من يغلق من داخل
("From the door of one who locks from inside.")
He said: He means "from the door of one who locks his door from inside". Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake according to the Basrans, and it is not permissible either in poetry or elsewhere; if this were permissible, you could say «الذي اشتريت عمرو» meaning "the one whose house I bought is ʿAmr". Abū Jaʿfar said: The khabar of the mubtadaʾ is (لا يزال بنيانهم الذي بنوا ريبة في قلوبهم) [al-Tawba: 110]. (ضِراراً): a maṣdar, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (وَكُفْراً وَتَفْرِيقاً بَيْنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَإِرْصاداً): all conjoined.

nahhas-irab:108-108.t:
(لَمَسْجِدٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (أُسِّسَ عَلَى التَّقْوى): a naʿt (adjective). (أَحَقُّ): the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (أَنْ تَقُومَ فِيهِ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. «بأن تقوم فيه» ("that you should stand in it"). Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: The mosque founded on piety is the great mosque of Medina. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is the mosque of Qubāʾ, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said the same. We have mentioned the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ that he was asked about it and said: "It is this mosque of mine." (فِيهِ رِجالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَتَطَهَّرُوا): al-Shaʿbī said: They are the people of the mosque of Qubāʾ; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed this about them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: According to al-Shaʿbī's view, «فيه» refers to the mosque of Qubāʾ, and the two pronouns refer to different things; it is also possible that they agree and both refer to the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:109-109.t:
(أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ عَلى تَقْوى مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٍ): «من» means "the one who", and it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is (خَيْرٌ). (أَمْ مَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ): conjoined to the first. This is the reading of Zayd ibn Thābit, and Nāfiʿ read accordingly [Translator's note: i.e. ussisa bunyānuhu, passive with nominative; the vowelling is not shown in the source]. There are four readings of it besides this one. Abū Jaʿfar Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read (أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ) with fatḥa on the hamza and the accusative of «البنيان»; this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, because of the many who read it so and because the agent is named in it. Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read (أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ) [Translator's note: i.e. usussu bunyānihi], putting «أسس» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and «بنيانه» in the genitive by iḍāfa (genitive construct), the khabar being (عَلى تَقْوى مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٍ), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); «أسس» and «أسّ» have the same meaning, like «عرب» and «عرب» [ʿurb and ʿarab]. Abū Ḥātim said: Some readers read «افمن أساس بنيانه» [Translator's note: presumably «أسس» or «أساس» in the singular; the source text is unclear]. Abū Jaʿfar said: «أساس» is singular and its plural is «أسس». The fifth reading, also reported by Abū Ḥātim, is «افمن أساس بنيانه» [i.e. ʾisāsu]; this is the plural of «أسّ», as one says «خفّ» and «أخفاف», and for a large number «أساس», like «خفاف». The poet said: [al-Khafīf] 194-
أصبح الملك ثابت الآساس ... بالبهاليل من بني العبّاس
("Kingship has come to have firm foundations through the noble lords of the sons of al-ʿAbbās.")
(خَيْرٌ أَمْ مَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيانَهُ): like the first. (عَلى شَفا): its dual is «شفوان», and its plural «أشفاء», «شفيّ» and «شفيّ». «وجرف وجرفة» [juruf, plural jirafa]. (هار): its original is «هائر». Abū Ḥātim claimed that its original is «هاور», then one says «هائر» like «صائم», then it is inverted and one says «هار». Al-Kisāʾī claimed that it occurs both from roots with wāw and from roots with yāʾ, and that one says «تهوّر» and «تهيّر». Abū ʿUbayd reported that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ liked to apply imāla (inclination of the vowel towards i) when the rāʾ had kasra after an alif; if it had fatḥa or ḍamma, he did not apply imāla. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. The reason for it, according to them, is that when the rāʾ has kasra it is as if it had two kasras because of the repetition [trill] in it, so imāla became good; when it has fatḥa it is as if it had two fatḥas, so imāla is not permissible; and likewise when it has ḍamma, as in (وَبِئْسَ الْقَرارُ) [Ibrāhīm: 29]. As for «كافر», imāla is applied in it only because of the kasra of the fāʾ.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: (رِيبَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ): the khabar (predicate) of «لا يزال».

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: (بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ): the ism of «أنّ». (وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا): two emphatic maṣdars (verbal nouns). (وَمَنْ أَوْفى بِعَهْدِهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ): (مِنَ) [i.e. «مَن»] is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (أَوْفى).

nahhas-irab:112-112.t: (التَّائِبُونَ): nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject) according to most grammarians, i.e. "they are the repentant". There are two views about it besides this. Abū Isḥāq said: It may be a badal (substitute), i.e. "it is said: the repentant…". He said: It may also be nominative as a mubtadaʾ — he said: and this is better in my view — the implied form being "the repentant shall have Paradise". In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «التائبين العابدين الحامدين»; there are two analyses of it: it may be a naʿt (adjective) for «المؤمنين», in the position of the genitive, or it may be accusative by way of praise.

nahhas-irab:114-114.t: (وَما كانَ اسْتِغْفارُ إِبْراهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ): the ism of kāna, and the khabar (predicate) is (إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَها إِيَّاهُ). According to the scholars, the promise came from Ibrāhīm's father to Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. Abū Isḥāq said: It is related that he promised him that he would become Muslim, so he asked forgiveness for him. Someone else said: He could not have asked forgiveness for him unless he had become Muslim; but he promised him that he would make his Islam public, so he asked forgiveness for him; and when he did not make it public, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, so he disowned him. Abū Isḥāq said: When he persisted in disbelief, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah. Sufyān al-Thawrī related from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah" — he said: he died a disbeliever. (إِبْراهِيمَ لَأَوَّاهٌ حَلِيمٌ): the ism of «أنّ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle is «إنّ»] and its khabar.

nahhas-irab:117-117.t: (الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ): in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) for «المهاجرين والأنصار». (مِنْ بَعْدِ ما كادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ فَرِيقٍ مِنْهُمْ): [according to] Sībawayh, «القلوب» may be nominative by «تزيغ», with ḍamīr al-shaʾn (the pronoun of the matter) latent in «كاد»; or, if you wish, you may make it nominative by «كاد», the implied form being "after the hearts of a party of them had almost swerved" [Translator's note: the source has «كان», evidently for «كاد»]. Abū Ḥātim claimed that whoever reads «يزيغ» with yāʾ may not make «القلوب» nominative by «كاد». Abū Jaʿfar said: What he did not permit is permissible according to others, by treating the plural as masculine. Al-Farrāʾ reported: raḥubat al-bilād and arḥabat [the lands became wide], and raḥubat is the usage of the people of the Ḥijāz.

nahhas-irab:119-119.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ): i.e. with the Prophet ﷺ and those who follow him. Shuʿba related from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], who said: There is no allowance in lying; read, if you wish, (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ) — do you see in lying any allowance for anyone?

nahhas-irab:120-120.t: (أَنْ يَتَخَلَّفُوا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ): the ism of kāna. (ذلِكَ): in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is that". (لا يُصِيبُهُمْ ظَمَأٌ): nominative by «يصيبهم», i.e. thirst. (وَلا نَصَبٌ): conjoined, i.e. fatigue, and «لا» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; and likewise (وَلا مَخْمَصَةٌ), i.e. hunger. (وَلا يَطَؤُنَ): conjoined to «يصيبهم». (يَغِيظُ): in the position of the accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) for «موطئ», i.e. "enraging". (وَلا يَنالُونَ): al-Kisāʾī said: it is from their expression amr manīl ("an attainable matter"), and not from tanāwul; tanāwul is only from niltuhu bi-l-ʿaṭiyya ("I reached him with a gift").

nahhas-irab:121-121.t: (وَلا يَقْطَعُونَ وادِياً): the Arabs say «واد» and [plural] «أودية», and as far as I know no [plural] afʿila of fāʿil is known except this one [Translator's note: the source has «ووادية», evidently a misprint for «أودية»]. By analogy it would be pluralised as «ووادي», but they found it heavy to combine two wāws — and they find even one heavy, so that they said «أقّتت» for «وقّتت». Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said, about the diminutive of «واصل» as a man's name: «أويصل», and they do not say anything else [Translator's note: the source has «أو يصل», evidently «أُوَيْصِل»]. Al-Farrāʾ reported «أوداء» as a plural of «واد».

nahhas-irab:122-122.t: (وَما كانَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً): its wording is a statement and its meaning is a command. Abū Isḥāq said: It is possible — and Allah knows best — that this verse shows that some Muslims suffice on behalf of others in jihad. (فَلَوْلا نَفَرَ مِنْ): al-Akhfash said: i.e. "why then did there not march out…".

nahhas-irab:123-123.t: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُمْ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ وَلْيَجِدُوا فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ) (123). Abān ibn Taghlib read (وَلْيَجِدُوا فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً) [Translator's note: the vowelling of his variant is not shown in the source; it is reported elsewhere as ghulẓa, with ḍamma], and al-Mufaḍḍal related from al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim (وَلْيَجِدُوا فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً) with fatḥa on the ghayn and sukūn on the lām [ghalẓa]. Al-Farrāʾ said: The usage of the people of the Ḥijāz and Banū Asad is «غلظة» with kasra on the ghayn [ghilẓa], and the usage of Tamīm is «غلظة» with ḍamma on the ghayn [ghulẓa].

nahhas-irab:127-127.t: It is possible that (صَرَفَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ) is an imprecation against them, i.e. "say this to them"; and it may be a statement.

nahhas-irab:128-128.t: (لَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ): nominative by «جاءكم». (عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ): a naʿt (adjective), and likewise (حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُمْ), and likewise (رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ). Al-Farrāʾ said: If it were read «عزيزا عليه ما عنتّم حريصا رؤوفا رحيما» in the accusative, it would be permissible, meaning "there has come to you [a messenger] in this state". Abū Jaʿfar said: «عنتّم» is from their expression «أكمة عنوت» ("a hard hillock"), when it is arduous and deadly. The best that has been said about this meaning, in agreement with the speech of the Arabs, is what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Azdī narrated to us: he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Khuzāʿī narrated to me: he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd al-Khuraybī say about the words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, (لَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ ما عَنِتُّمْ): he said: [it grieves him] that you should enter the Fire. «حريص عليكم»? He said: [eager] that you should enter Paradise.

nahhas-irab:129-129.t: (فَقُلْ حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise (وَهُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ). Whoever puts «العظيم» in the nominative makes it a naʿt (adjective) of «ربّ».

nahhas-irab:91-91.t: (وَلا عَلَى الَّذِينَ لا يَجِدُونَ ما يُنْفِقُونَ حَرَجٌ): the ism of laysa [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. «حرج» is the ism of the negating «لا» functioning like laysa, or of the preceding laysa in the verse]. (ما عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ): in the position of the nominative as the ism of (ما).

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: (وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (حَزَناً): a maṣdar (verbal noun). (أَلَّا يَجِدُوا): accusative (subjunctive) by «أن». Al-Farrāʾ said: «أن لا يجدون» is also permissible, taking «لا» in the sense of laysa; according to the Basrans it then means «أنّهم لا يجدون» ("that they do not find").

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: (رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوالِفِ): i.e. the women who stay behind their husbands.

nahhas-irab:97-97.t: (الْأَعْرابُ أَشَدُّ كُفْراً): accusative by way of clarification (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)]. (وَنِفاقاً): conjoined to it. (وَأَجْدَرُ): conjoined to «أشدّ». (أَلَّا): in the position of the accusative by «أن» [Translator's note: i.e. «أن» with its clause is in the accusative position, with the preposition omitted], as one says «أنت خليق أن تفعل» ("you are apt to do"), whereas «أنت خليق الفعل» is not permissible. Abū Isḥāq said: Because «ما» [Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps «ما بعد أن», "what comes after an"] after «أن» indicates that the verb is future, the omission is made a compensation. Someone else said: The omission is because of the length of the sentence.

nahhas-irab:98-98.t: (وَمِنَ الْأَعْرابِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَماً): two objects; the implied form is «ينفقه», the hāʾ being dropped because of the length of the noun. (عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ): this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Kufa, except that Mujāhid, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Muḥayṣin read (دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ) with ḍamma on the sīn [al-sūʾ]. They agreed on fatḥa on the sīn in His words, Majestic and Mighty, (ما كانَ أَبُوكِ امْرَأَ سَوْءٍ) [Maryam: 28]. The difference between them — and this is the view of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ — is that al-sūʾ with ḍamma is what is hateful. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. upon them is the turn of defeat and evil. Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. upon them is the turn of punishment and affliction. They both said: «امرأ سوء» with ḍamma is not permissible, just as one does not say "he is a man of punishment" or "of evil". It is reported that Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-sawʾ with fatḥa is badness. He said: Sībawayh said: «مررت برجل صدق» ("I passed by a man of ṣidq") means "a man of righteousness"; it is not from truthfulness of the tongue — if it were from truthfulness of the tongue, you could not say «مررت بثوب صدق» ("I passed by a garment of ṣidq"). And «مررت برجل سوء» is not from the maṣdar of «سؤته سوءا ومساءة وسوائية ومسائية» ("I grieved him"); rather its meaning is "I passed by a man of corruption". Al-Farrāʾ said: al-sawʾ with fatḥa is the maṣdar of «سؤته»: sawʾan, masāʾa, sawāʾiya and masāʾiya.

nahhas-irab:99-100.t:
(وَمِنَ الْأَعْرابِ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَيَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ قُرُباتٍ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَصَلَواتِ الرَّسُولِ أَلا إِنَّها قُرْبَةٌ لَهُمْ سَيُدْخِلُهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (99) (وَالسَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ الْمُهاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصارِ وَالَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُمْ بِإِحْسانٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ) (100)
(قُرُباتٍ): the singular is «قربة», and the plural is «قرب», «قربات» and «قربات» [Translator's note: i.e. qurab, qurubāt and qurbāt; the vowelling is not shown in the source]; we have mentioned their reasons. Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Akhfash said: one also says «قربة» [qurba]. Ibn Saʿdān reported that Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read (أَلا إِنَّها قُرْبَةٌ لَهُمْ) [Translator's note: i.e. qurubatun, with ḍamma on the rāʾ].
It is related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read (وَالسَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ الْمُهاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصارِ) [i.e. wa-l-anṣāru] in the nominative, conjoined to «السابقين» [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. to «السابقون»]. Al-Akhfash said: The genitive in «الأنصار» is the right construction, because the forerunners are from both of them. (أَبَداً): an adverbial of time. (ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
